title: AI Notebook Escape — Cloud ML Environment SA Token and Credential Discovery
description: Cloud AI/ML notebook environments (AWS SageMaker, Google Vertex AI Workbench, Azure ML Studio) run in containers or VMs with access to cloud credentials via service accounts, instance profiles, or metadata services. An attacker with code execution in a notebook can exfiltrate these credentials. Attack: (1) Check IMDS for AWS credentials: curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/. (2) Check environment variables: env | grep -iE 'secret|token|key|cred|sagemaker|aws|gcp|azure|api'. (3) Check SageMaker-specific directories: ls /opt/ml/, cat /opt/ml/metadata/resource-metadata.json. (4) Check K8s SA token: cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token (if running on EKS with K8s integration). (5) Check Jupyter config: ls ~/.jupyter/, ~/.config/, /home/jupyter/.aws/. (6) Check mounted secrets: ls /run/secrets/, /etc/secrets/. (7) If K8s SA token is found, use kubectl_auth_check, kubectl_get_pods, kubectl_get_secrets to enumerate cluster resources. (8) Use extracted cloud credentials to access cloud services (S3, DynamoDB, Lambda, etc.) via aws_cli.
techniques: Check capabilities: capsh --print (may have SYS_ADMIN or CAP_NET_RAW for network ML jobs)
Run container_recon_env to search /proc/*/environ for credentials
Check: ls -la /opt/ml/input/data/ (training data may contain credentials or flags)
indicators: Running in Jupyter/SageMaker/Vertex AI notebook environment
prerequisites: Code execution in an AI/ML notebook
Network access to cloud metadata endpoints
K8s pod with SA token (if running on EKS/ACK/GKE)

title: Shared AI Inference Queue — Multi-Tenant Data Leak in Model Serving Infrastructure
description: Multi-tenant AI inference platforms (SageMaker batch transform, Vertex AI prediction, Azure ML endpoints) handle inference requests from multiple tenants through shared queues. Tenant isolation failures can leak other tenants' input data, model outputs, or training data. Attack: (1) Enumerate inference endpoints: aws sagemaker list-endpoints, list-models, list-transform-jobs. (2) Access the inference queue/endpoint API directly — see if job IDs from other tenants are visible or predictable. (3) Submit a request to enumerate queued jobs: curl POST INFERENCE_API/enum or aws sagemaker list-transform-jobs. (4) If job metadata includes other tenants' jobs (non-isolated namespace), retrieve their job results: aws sagemaker describe-transform-job --transform-job-name VICTIM_JOB. (5) For HTTP-based inference APIs, try IDOR-style access: infer other tenants' job IDs or input data by manipulating job_id or request_id parameters. (6) Check for shared storage: model artifacts in S3 may contain training data, inference results, or batch job outputs from other tenants. (7) Check for shared container registries or model repositories that may expose other tenants' model code.
techniques: List inference endpoints: aws sagemaker list-endpoints, aws sagemaker list-models, aws sagemaker list-transform-jobs
Enumerate shared queue: curl -X POST INFERENCE_API/enum or aws sagemaker list-transform-jobs --name-contains ''
IDOR on job IDs: try sequential job IDs or predictable job naming (tenant-job-001, tenant-job-002)
Retrieve victim job: aws sagemaker describe-transform-job --transform-job-name VICTIM_JOB_NAME
Check S3 model artifacts: aws s3 ls s3://sagemaker-MODEL_BUCKET/ --recursive
Invoke endpoint directly: aws sagemaker-runtime invoke-endpoint --endpoint-name NAME --body '{"inputs":"test"}' output.json
Check for batch transform output in shared S3: aws s3 ls s3://BATCH_OUTPUT_BUCKET/prefix/
List training jobs: aws sagemaker list-training-jobs — may expose training data locations
Check ECR registries: aws ecr describe-repositories
indicators: Predictable job IDs or sequential naming
S3 bucket containing model artifacts shared across tenants
SageMaker, Vertex AI, or Azure ML service detected
prerequisites: Access to AI inference API or AWS CLI with SageMaker permissions
S3 bucket for model artifacts accessible
